jobs.label: Project record and evidence handoff
jobs.description: Carry one project record, its geography, linked evidence, review state, and exact files into a retained evidence package.

jobs.label: Land-use plan
jobs.description: Author, review, adopt, publish, and retain a statutory land-use plan under the applicable jurisdiction bundle.

jobs.label: Safety analysis
jobs.description: Acquire observed crash records for a project area, disclose source coverage, and retain the safety evidence.

jobs.label: Grants and reimbursement
jobs.description: Find applicable programs, preserve source limits, and carry an award through delivery and reimbursement records.

jobs.label: Model validation evidence
jobs.description: Open a genuine baseline, inspect separate AequilibraE and ActivitySim assessments, and download exact scientific evidence.

claims.applicability: The jurisdiction-neutral project record and immutable handoff are available. California-specific legal sufficiency is outside this claim.
limitations: The evidence package is a retained snapshot, not approval, adoption, publication, or a backup.

claims.applicability: A configured California general-plan descriptor supplies cited statewide requirements and process steps.

authorities.label: California Government Code, Article 5: Authority for and Scope of General Plans
California Government Code, Article 6: Preparation, Adoption, and Amendment
California Government Code, Article 8: Specific Plans

The installed workflow still uses the general-plan checklist for specific plans. Separate specific-plan rules are prepared but are not yet connected to production routes and forms.

Frozen versions preserve their retained rules. Earlier drafts still need explicit checklist reconciliation that preserves existing content.

limitations: The result is inconclusive, the modeled quantity is synthetic expanded daily traffic, and neither method is validated for planner accuracy claims.

claims.applicability: ODOT's published crash layer supplies located Oregon crashes with KABCO severity for live reads and corridor runs. FARS supplies the fatal-only records a Safety acquisition stores.

authorities.label: Oregon Transportation Safety Data Explorer crash data

limitations: The ODOT crash layer is read live and not stored: safety_crashes does not admit its source id, so a Safety acquisition in Oregon still stores fatal-only FARS records.

ODOT states no access constraints but names no open license. Crashes ODOT could not locate are excluded, and the layer holds only the years ODOT publishes in it (2019 to 2024 when checked on November 1, 2026).

claims.applicability: Federal and Oregon program descriptors can be matched to the workspace jurisdiction.
limitations: The catalog is not a live opportunity feed, and OpenPlan does not yet ship an Oregon reimbursement procedure profile.

claims.applicability: The v0.41 comparable-observation development registry contains California counties only.
limitations: No Oregon use-specific model validation assessment is available.

claims.applicability: The jurisdiction-neutral project record and evidence package can retain a Puerto Rico place of record without inheriting state rules.
limitations: One v0.42 Puerto Rico readiness journey is frozen as release evidence; a complete territory-specific project handoff remains unproven.

claims.applicability: OpenPlan has no configured Puerto Rico statutory plan bundle.
limitations: The product must not substitute California, another state, or a generic legal checklist.

claims.applicability: FARS supplies Puerto Rico fatal crash records for 2020 through 2024 from NHTSA's separate Puerto Rico annual file.
limitations: The adapter is fatal-only and persists retrieved crash records. It cannot support an all-severity or serious-injury claim.

NHTSA's Puerto Rico files for 2010 through 2019 carry no crash coordinates, so OpenPlan reads Puerto Rico from 2020 on and treats an earlier year as not answered. Checked 2026-11-01: 6 of 229 crashes in 2020 and 1 of 330 in 2021 have no coordinates and cannot be placed in a study area.

claims.applicability: No Puerto Rico-specific program or reimbursement profile is registered.
limitations: Country-level catalog entries are not enough to claim program eligibility or reimbursement procedure coverage in Puerto Rico.

claims.applicability: The current comparable-observation study has no Puerto Rico geography.
limitations: No Puerto Rico use-specific model validation assessment is available.
